s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute to chronic swelling and pain over the clavicular area with a tender mass and overlying skin changes
salient_findings: 6-month history of swelling and moderate pain over the left clavicular area
Tender 2 × 3 cm swelling over the left clavicle with a small clean overlying wound and erythema
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 50 mm/h
Midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture on chest radiograph
key_facts: 9-year-old boy
6-month history of symptoms
No fever, weight loss, or trauma
Received unspecified oral medications for one month at another center
Normal vital signs
Tender swelling over the left clavicle
Small clean overlying wound and erythema
Preserved shoulder range of motion
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 50 mm/h
Normal complete blood count, renal and liver function tests
Unremarkable abdominal ultrasound
Midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture on chest radiograph
Clear lung fields on chest radiograph

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a tender swelling over the clavicle with a lytic expansile lesion and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the chronic nature of symptoms and the presence of a tender mass with overlying skin changes

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the lytic expansile lesion and the elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, although less common in this age group

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely given the age and location, osteosarcoma is a possible consideration given the aggressive nature of the lesion

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a consideration given the expansile nature of the lesion, although typically presents with more pronounced bone destruction

raw.rationale: The presence of a midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture, along with an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and a 6-month history of swelling and moderate pain, is most consistent with Ewing's sarcoma, a malignant bone tumor that can present with similar radiographic and clinical findings.

rejected.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While chronic osteomyelitis could explain some of the symptoms, the presence of a lytic expansile lesion and the lack of fever or discharge make it less likely.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: This condition can cause lytic bone lesions, but it is less likely given the age of the patient and the specific location and characteristics of the lesion.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Osteosarcoma is a malignant bone tumor, but it typically presents with more aggressive features and is less common in the clavicle.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are benign lesions that can cause expansile bone lesions, but they are less likely to cause systemic symptoms like an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
